hypothesis: A TRAIN-selected small-block incremental GF2 elimination representation can replace multiple individual XOR eliminations on related unknown causal state constraints with one exact precompiled reduction lookup per block, lowering real row-elimination XOR counts and whole-process CPU without increasing peak RSS versus optimized exact scalar incremental GF2.
mechanism: TRAIN sees ONLY public equation masks from synthetic source-free streams and ranks pivot coordinate frequency/co-occurrence. It chooses compact 3-4 bit pivot groups. Online candidate retains an exact triangular GF2 basis; per-block row-reduction tables are exact algebraic lookup transforms, rebuilt when basis pivots enter a group. Lookup reduces several already-known pivots with a single XOR. An unrecognized pivot falls back to scalar exact elimination. Unlike T34, this must reduce actual GF2 XOR update operations, not just factor merges.

sourcefree_stress.public_masks: sparse 2-4 bit within correlated eight-variable modules with occasional cross-module rows and repeated constraints
sourcefree_stress.rhs: exact independent hidden vector only used to generate consistent public equations; hidden vector never passed to learning or inference
sourcefree_stress.source_free_independent_exact: independent lower-pivot canonical batch Gaussian rebuilder verifies each query

required_tests.learned_parameter_ablation: Learned grouping ON versus fixed grouping OFF must demonstrably change actual block lookup XOR reductions, with completely identical certified answers and no false positives
required_tests.actual_xor_reduction: count all basis-update XORs PLUS all LUT reconstruction XORs and all per-query transformations; strictly fewer than optimized exact incremental baseline on source-free validation before looking at native performance
